subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept the exact `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`/`node-pty` dependency graph and MXC SDK argv-carried config boundary for this official external Windows sandbox plugin after the registration-mode fix lands?
rationale: The code can mechanically fix the registration-mode side effect, but accepting native sandbox executor binaries, install scripts, and base64 config exposure through process argv is a maintainer/security boundary decision.

options.title: Approve After Registration Fix
options.body: Fix MXC to register runtime hooks only in full mode, then approve the exact dependency graph and argv boundary for this opt-in external plugin.

options.title: Pause For Safer SDK Transport
options.body: Hold the PR until upstream MXC or OpenClaw provides a config transport that does not expose the encoded sandbox envelope through argv.

options.title: Incubate Outside First-Party Release
options.body: Keep MXC outside the official OpenClaw release path until the native dependency and sandbox boundary are mature enough for first-party support.

recommendation.title: Approve After Registration Fix
recommendation.body: Fix MXC to register runtime hooks only in full mode, then approve the exact dependency graph and argv boundary for this opt-in external plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the live assignee and CODEOWNERS-backed route for the remaining release/security acceptance call.
